comments.text: its full stack developments ive been a full stack engineer for 10 years now and I worked for a big insurance software company, this was before AI came out back in 2016 I was using Ubot Studio to create large automations and using UI Path, (which is pretty much n8n broken down into thousands of pieces I hate thinking about making a new bot scraper.) and I worked with a team on 10 engineers just within our team 10 of us handled a small portion of this huge companies software and one handled SQL, a couple others handld  .NET API integrations  then couple of us handled REACT frontend... They laid off 150 engineers in Jan 2024 to outsource out job to the Philipines., at that time I was using GPT-3.5 and claude 2 and thought it was amazing, to help with automation and code structure, we never talked about AI as a team or company even though i brought it up, and looking back as I type this its insane how long it would take to create a API back then.. smh...  Come June 2024 I remember I was using Claude Opus-3.5 and GPT-4o and was hired at Arizona States Ira A. Fulton School of Engineering which is their largest school within ASU.  long story short  a few months ago i won the 2026 innovation Award out of all ASU employees which was a big overall milestone for me at least, but its been about 1.5 years since I built a full stack HRM system to hire student workers for them, Hires 900 students a semester over 500 professors use it, I just integrated another Program within the school and the Dean wants a whole campus every school within ASU to adapt it... Crazy part, its just me alone and AI. And I tell them in large meetings I need unlimited access to all AI possible unless your going to hire more developers and how if this was a project at my old job it would be at least 10 SR engineers working on this. But between Claude and Codex and the other 125 models, and 45 LLMs they gave me access to I (plus AI) have built everything from the ground up, Database, Backend (Python FastAPI), Frontend (react, ts, java) and to think it can do this (with there being some minor and some not so minor hiccups) blows my mind daily. I remember before I launched it I had the entire backend written in C# (ASP.NET) and had a meeting and was told they stopped supporting .NET a few months back. This was after at least 4 months endless programming. I'll never forget during that 1.5 hour meeting claude had converted the entire backend from C# to Python, reconfigured the frontend architecture, and connections. It is insane. But one thing "vibecoders" forget is it is beneficial to have true coding experience because I am able to tell claude or codex what to build using what Stack (languages, package libraries) to use, and all the different stacks which saves me a ton of tokens and time. AI I have tested gets it right maybe 80% of the time, I mean the app will work 100% of the time but the stacks it uses if you dont tell it specifically, sometimes it is not what the user should be implementing. And every time a student worker has me look over their work I can instantly tell they did no coding or even looked it over which is somewhat sad. And they dont realize that once its coding something you agree with it and stores it, it will continue to use the same packages and libraries when if they just did some true learning they could improve a good application into a great application.
